object.title: The one-firefighter containment conjecture for the strong grid
object.statement: The strong grid is the graph obtained from the square grid by joining vertices that are at king-move distance one, so each vertex is adjacent also to its diagonal neighbours. In the Pyro game, firefighters protect vertices while the fire spreads to unprotected neighbouring vertices. **Strong-grid containment conjecture.** In the Pyro game, one firefighter cannot contain a fire on the strong grid. The source states that two firefighters suffice, while whether one firefighter suffices remains unknown; it therefore conjectures that one firefighter is insufficient.
object.source_name: Margaret-Ellen Messinger and Spencer Yarnell, “The Pyro game: a slow intelligent fire”, arXiv:2108.00101 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.00101

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2021).

object.title: Katznelson's recurrence conjecture for countably infinite abelian groups
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a countably infinite abelian group. A set $S\subseteq G$ is a **set of Bohr recurrence** if it intersects every Bohr neighborhood of $0$, and it is a **set of chromatic recurrence** if the Cayley graph determined by $S$ has infinite chromatic number.

**Katznelson's conjecture.** If $S\subseteq G$ is a set of Bohr recurrence, then $S$ is a set of chromatic recurrence.

This is the general form of a question suggested by Veech and popularized by Katznelson. No countably infinite abelian group is currently known for which the answer is settled.
object.source_name: John T. Griesmer, “Special cases and equivalent forms of Katznelson's problem on recurrence”, arXiv:2108.02190 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.02190

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2021).

object.title: Polynomial χ-boundedness of grounded segment graphs
object.statement: A **grounded segment graph** is the intersection graph of a collection of line segments grounded on a common line. **Grounded segment-graph conjecture.** The class of grounded segment graphs is polynomially χ-bounded. Grounded segment graphs are a class of geometric intersection graphs; the conjecture asks whether their chromatic number is bounded by a polynomial in their clique number, extending the polynomial χ-boundedness results discussed for related grounded classes. The source presents this as an open question and gives no resolution.
object.source_name: James Davies, Tomasz Krawczyk, Rose McCarty and Bartosz Walczak, “Grounded L-graphs are polynomially χ-bounded”, arXiv:2108.05611 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.05611

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2021).

object.title: Exponential resistance growth conjecture for square grid graphs
object.statement:
Let $G=P_n\square P_n$ be the $n\times n$ grid graph with $n^2$ vertices, and let $H=P_{n+1}\square P_{n+1}$ be the $(n+1)\times(n+1)$ grid graph with $(n+1)^2$ vertices. Let $r_G(a,b)$ and $r_H(a,b)$ denote the resistance distances between the indicated vertices, and let $r_n(a,b)$ denote the corresponding resistance distance in the $n\times n$ grid. **Square grid resistance growth conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty}\left(\exp(r_H(a,b))-\exp(r_G(a,b))\right)=C>0.
$$

Moreover,

$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty}r_n(a,b)=\infty.
$$

The conjecture asserts exponential growth of resistance distance under successive square-grid enlargements, together with divergence of the resistance distance. The source gives empirical evidence but does not establish the claim.
object.source_name: E. J. Evans and A. E. Francis, “Algorithmic techniques for finding resistance distances on structured graphs”, arXiv:2108.07942 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.07942

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2021).

object.title: Exponential resistance growth conjecture for triangular grid graphs
object.statement:
Let $T_n$ be the triangular grid graph shown in Figure~, with $n$ rows and $m=n^2$ cells. Let $a$ and $b$ be distinct vertices of degree $2$, and let $r_n(a,b)$ be the resistance distance between $a$ and $b$ in $T_n$. **Triangular grid resistance growth conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty}\left(\exp(r_{n+1}(a,b))-\exp(r_n(a,b))\right)=C>0.
$$

Moreover,

$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty}r_n(a,b)=\infty.
$$

The conjecture predicts exponential growth of resistance distance between fixed degree-$2$ vertices as the triangular grid expands, and in particular divergence of that resistance distance. The source offers empirical evidence but no proof.
object.source_name: E. J. Evans and A. E. Francis, “Algorithmic techniques for finding resistance distances on structured graphs”, arXiv:2108.07942 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.07942

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2021).

object.title: Wang–Zhou conjecture on realizations of abstract topological recursion
object.statement: Let $4\mathcal W_{g,n}4$ be the abstract $n$-point functions of the abstract quantum field theory of fat graphs. Under a suitable Feynman-rule realization, let $4\mathcal C4$ be the realized spectral curve and let $B(x_1,x_2)$ be the realization of the abstract Bergmann kernel $4\mathcal W_{0,2}4$. **Wang–Zhou's topological-recursion conjecture.** The Eynard–Orantin invariants associated to $4\mathcal C4$ and $B(x_1,x_2)$ are the realizations of the abstract $n$-point functions $4\mathcal W_{g,n}4$. This is established for the Hermitian one-matrix model and fat-graph enumeration, while the general realization problem remains open.
object.source_name: Zhiyuan Wang and Jian Zhou, “A formalism of abstract quantum field theory of summation of fat graphs”, arXiv:2108.10498 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.10498

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2021).

object.title: Wang–Zhou conjecture on residue reformulation of abstract topological recursion
object.statement: Let $4\mathcal W_{g,n}4$ be the abstract $n$-point functions and let the abstract quantum field theory have spectral curve $4\mathcal C4$. **Wang–Zhou's residue-reformulation conjecture.** The abstract $n$-point functions can be modified as multilinear differentials on $4\mathcal C4$ so that the quadratic recursion can be reformulated using formal residues, and the realization of this recursion is equivalent to Eynard–Orantin topological recursion. This would provide an intrinsic geometric formulation of the abstract recursion; it is conjectural beyond the examples discussed in the paper.
object.source_name: Zhiyuan Wang and Jian Zhou, “A formalism of abstract quantum field theory of summation of fat graphs”, arXiv:2108.10498 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.10498

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2021).

object.title: Symmetry conjecture for fully commutative elements in rank-two Shephard groups
object.statement: Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers. In the notation $a[b]a$ for the rank-two Shephard group with endpoint parameters $a,a$ and braid parameter $b$, and $b[a]b$ for the group with these parameters exchanged, consider fully commutative elements having a unique reduced expression, enumerated by their length. **Rank-two symmetry conjecture.** The enumeration by length is identical for the groups $a[b]a$ and $b[a]b$. This conjecture arises from enumeration tables for exceptional Shephard groups; the supplied source gives no proof or resolution.
object.source_name: Jiayuan Wang, “A note on fully commutative elements in complex reflection groups”, arXiv:2109.09773 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.09773

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2021).

object.title: Luschny's permanent conjecture for median Genocchi numbers
object.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and define the $2n\times 2n$ matrix

$$
M_{2n}:=\left[\left\lfloor\frac{2j-k-1}{2n}\right\rfloor\right]_{1\le j,k\le 2n}.
$$

The **Luschny permanent conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{per}(M_{2n})=(-1)^nH_{2n-1}.
$$

Here $H_1,H_3,H_5,\ldots$ are the Genocchi numbers of the second kind, or median Genocchi numbers. The conjecture was proposed by P. Luschny and is one of the five permanent conjectures proved in the paper, so it is solved.
object.source_name: Shishuo Fu, Zhicong Lin and Zhi-Wei Sun, “Permanent identities, combinatorial sequences, and permutation statistics”, arXiv:2109.11506 (2024).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.11506

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of September 2021); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

object.title: Bipartite analogue of the Jaeger–Zhang conjecture
object.statement:
Let $p$ be a positive integer, and let $\mathcal{P}^*_{4p}$ denote the class of signed bipartite planar graphs with the indicated girth condition. **Bipartite analogue of the Jaeger–Zhang conjecture.**

$$
\chi_c(\mathcal{P}^*_{4p})\leq \frac{4p}{2p-1}.
$$

This is a modified bipartite analogue of the Jaeger–Zhang conjecture, proposed in light of a later result cited by the paper. The surrounding discussion treats it as an open conjecture and notes related expected bounds for neighboring indices.
object.source_name: Reza Naserasr and Zhouningxin Wang, “Signed bipartite circular cliques and a bipartite analogue of Grötzsch's theorem”, arXiv:2109.12618 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.12618

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2021). “Beside all the open questions that are summarized in the table, there are two questions of interest to mention.”

object.title: Extremality conjecture for substituted planar triangulations
object.statement:
Let $\ell\ge 7$. Let $G$ be a dense graph of girth $\ell+1$, and let $B$ be an $n$-vertex planar triangulation with no $\ell$-cycle, chosen to maximize $n$. Form $G'$ by substituting $B$ into $G$, and write $n'=|V(G')|$. **Extremality conjecture.** The substituted construction is extremal, namely

$$
\operatorname{ex}_{\mathcal{P}}(n',C_{\ell})=|E(G')|.
$$

The paper states that this may be plausible for some small values of $\ell$ but appears difficult to prove in general.
object.source_name: Daniel W. Cranston, Bernard Lidický, Xiaonan Liu and Abhinav Shantanam, “Planar Turán Numbers of Cycles: A Counterexample”, arXiv:2110.02043 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.02043

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

object.title: Pattern conjecture for eigenvalues in the perfect matchings association scheme
object.statement:
Consider the perfect matchings association scheme on $K_{2k}$, with classes indexed by partitions and modules indexed by partitions. For an integer $i$, let $[2k-2i,2i]$ and $[2k-2i,2,\ldots,2]$ denote the indicated modules.

**Eigenvalue pattern conjecture.** The eigenvalues of the class $[2k]$ corresponding to these modules are, respectively,

$$
-(2i-3)!!(2k-2i-2)!!
$$

and

$$
(-1)^i(i!)(2k-2i-2)!!.
$$

The statement records patterns observed in the character tables of the perfect matchings association scheme. The source presents them as further work rather than proving them, and gives no resolution beyond the displayed formulas.
object.source_name: Mahsa N. Shirazi, “An extension of the Erdős-Ko-Rado theorem to set-wise 2-intersecting families of perfect matchings”, arXiv:2110.02175 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.02175

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

object.title: Brenti–Carnevale–Tenner's rank-symmetry conjecture for odd diagram classes
object.statement:
Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group on $[n]$. For $w\in S_n$, define its odd diagram by

$$
D_o(w)=\{(i,j)\colon w(i)>j,\ i<w^{-1}(j),\ i\not\equiv w^{-1}(j) \pmod 2\}.
$$

An odd diagram is a set $D=D_o(w)$, and its odd diagram class is

$$
\mathrm{Perm}(D)=\{w\in S_n\colon D_o(w)=D\}.
$$

**Brenti–Carnevale–Tenner's conjecture.** Each odd diagram class is rank-symmetric in the Bruhat order.

Odd diagram classes are known to be intervals in the Bruhat order. The conjecture asserts the stronger symmetry property that the ranks in each such interval are symmetric; the paper's abstract states that its results resolve this conjecture by factoring the associated Poincaré polynomial into factors of the form $1+t+\cdots+t^m$.
object.source_name: Neil J. Y. Fan and Peter L. Guo, “Poincaré Polynomials of Odd Diagram Classes”, arXiv:2110.04723 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.04723

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of October 2021); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

object.title: Gorenstein characterization conjecture for normal homogeneous subrings of graphs
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with homogeneous subring $S$, and assume that $S$ is normal. Say that $G$ is **unmixed** when all its relevant minimal vertex covers have the same cardinality, and let a **strong $\lceil\frac{n}{2}\rceil$-$\tau$-reduction** mean a strong reduction of the indicated size. **Gorenstein characterization conjecture.** Under the assumption that $S$ is normal,

$$
S\text{ is Gorenstein}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad G\text{ is unmixed with a strong }\left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil\text{-}\tau\text{-reduction}.
$$

This connects the commutative-algebraic property of being Gorenstein with a combinatorial reduction of the graph. The supplied parser gives no resolution evidence, so the conjectural characterization remains open here.
object.source_name: Lourdes Cruz, Enrique Reyes and Jonathan Toledo, “Gorenstein homogeneous subrings of graphs”, arXiv:2110.05253 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.05253

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

object.title: Milićević's cubic-curve conjecture for point-line configurations
object.statement:
Let $P$ be a set of $n$ points in general position in the plane, and let $R$ be a disjoint set of $n$ points. Assume that every line determined by two points of $P$ contains a point of $R$.

**Milićević's conjecture.** Then $P \cup R$ is contained in a cubic curve.

This conjecture concerns the extremal case of the lower bound $|R| \geq |P|$ for even $n>4$. The paper presents it as an open characterization problem; no resolution is supplied in the given text.
object.source_name: Mehdi Makhul and Rom Pinchasi, “On sets of points in general position that lie on a cubic curve in the plane and determine lines that can be pierced by few points”, arXiv:2110.06179 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06179

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of October 2021). “Conjecture is proved in under a similar additional assumption as in Theorem .”

object.title: The center conjecture for the affine partition algebra
object.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer, let $\mathcal{A}_{2k}^{\text{aff}}$ be the affine partition algebra, and let $z_l$ and $p_n$ denote the central elements introduced in the paper for $l,n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$. The center is denoted by $Z(\mathcal{A}_{2k}^{\text{aff}})$. **Center conjecture.**

$$
Z(\mathcal{A}_{2k}^{\text{aff}})=\langle z_l,p_n\mid l,n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}\rangle.
$$

This conjecture proposes that the displayed elements generate the whole center of the affine partition algebra, extending the description of the center of the finite partition algebra and paralleling results for other affine diagram algebras. Its resolution is not specified in the source.
object.source_name: Samuel Creedon and Maud De Visscher, “Defining an Affine Partition Algebra”, arXiv:2110.08652 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.08652

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

object.title: Conjecture on great-circle thrackleable trees and augmented caterpillars
object.statement: A **great-circle thrackleable tree** is a tree admitting a thrackle drawing on the sphere in which the edges are great-circle arcs. An **augmented caterpillar** is the graph class defined in the source. **Conjecture on great-circle thrackleable trees and augmented caterpillars.** The class of great-circle thrackleable trees is properly contained in the class of augmented caterpillars. The conjecture is proposed as a further restriction on the class of trees that can be great-circle thrackleable; the source leaves it open and notes that crossing orientations may be relevant to proving or disproving it.
object.source_name: Karen Collins and Cleo Roberts, “Great-circle Tree Thrackles”, arXiv:2110.09679 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.09679

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2021). “Despite its age and the many early advances by Douglas Woodall , the Thrackle Conjecture remains open.”

object.title: The star conjecture for big vertices in minimal-ABC trees
object.statement:
Let a minimal-ABC tree be a tree minimizing the atom-bond-connectivity index, and call its vertices of degree greater than one **big vertices**. Consider the subgraph induced by all big vertices.

**Star conjecture.** The subgraph of a minimal-ABC tree induced by its big vertices is a star.

This conjecture is attributed in the paper to earlier work and concerns the global structure of minimal-ABC trees. The supplied text gives no resolution status, so it remains open in this database.
object.source_name: Darko Dimitrov and Zhibin Du, “Complete characterization of the minimal-ABC trees”, arXiv:2110.14712 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.14712

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

object.title: Shin–Zeng's enumeration conjecture for signed Simsun permutations
object.statement:
Let ${{\mathcal{RS}}}{{\textrm{I}}}_n$ be the set of signed permutations whose underlying permutation is Simsun, and let ${{\mathcal{RS}}}{{\textrm{I}}}^{(B)}_n$ be the subset satisfying the positivity condition on right-to-left minima in absolute value. For $1\le k\le n$, define

$$
{{\mathcal{RS}}}{{\textrm{I}}}^{(B)}_{n,k}:=\{\sigma\in{{\mathcal{RS}}}{{\textrm{I}}}^{(B)}_n:\sigma_n=k\}.
$$

**Shin–Zeng's conjecture.** For $1\le k\le n$,

$$
v_{n,k}=\#{{\mathcal{RS}}}{{\textrm{I}}}^{(B)}_{n,n-k+1}.
$$

This is an enumerative question concerning the numbers $v_{n,k}$ and signed Simsun permutations of type I; the supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
object.source_name: Sen-Peng Eu and Tung-Shan Fu, “Springer Numbers and Arnold Families Revisited”, arXiv:2111.00888 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.00888

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2021).

object.title: Horizontal initial-position conjecture for Infinite Hex
object.statement:
Consider Infinite Hex played on its infinite board, with Red and Blue claiming tiles according to the usual rules. The initial position is the one depicted in Figure.

**Horizontal initial-position conjecture.** A game of Infinite Hex with initial position as in figure is a win for Red.

The source presents this as an apparently easier problem related to the conjecture that a single initial Red tile guarantees victory. It gives no proof or resolution, so the problem remains open.
object.source_name: Davide Leonessi, “Transfinite game values in infinite games”, arXiv:2111.01630 (2021).
